A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ANFR architecture and share the core experiments, equations, and figures. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite changes to the title, authorship, and organization.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments across five datasets, differential-privacy results, attention-module comparisons, and class-selectivity and localization analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds architecture comparisons, alternative training protocols, sensitivity analyses, convergence plots, and computational measurements.

M1.justification: ANFR remains the combination of scaled weight standardization and channel attention within an NF-ResNet backbone. Attention placement and the SE, ECA, and CBAM variants are retained. Testing different depths and initializations does not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use Fed-ISIC2019, FedChest, CIFAR-10, CelebA, and FedPathology for the same classification tasks, alongside ImageNet pretraining. The added experiments reuse this coverage; centralized controls, initialization choices, and hardware profiling change configurations rather than datasets or prediction tasks.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated FixBN comparisons on Fed-ISIC2019 and FedChest in Table 3; v1 only discussed FixBN as related work. Section 4.8 and Table 9 substantially broaden the architectural comparators to EfficientNetV2-Small, ViT-Small, ConvNeXt-Small, and FedConv-InvertUp, beyond the retained ResNet variants.

E3.justification: v2 adds doubled-local-step experiments, the nine-round FLamby protocol, random-initialization and centralized controls, final-round CIFAR-10 evaluation with batch size 64 and no gradient clipping, and CPU/GPU profiling. Section 4.1 also changes the stated CIFAR-10 client count from eight to five while retaining split-2 and the numerical table entries. This establishes a reported setting change without establishing that those experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained attention-module, CSI, attention-weight, and localization analyses, v2 tests sensitivity to local training steps, pretraining, benchmark hyperparameters, checkpoint selection, and FedChest batch size (Section 4.2; Appendices B and C.3). It also adds convergence trajectories and measured computational overhead, substantially expanding scrutiny of robustness and practicality.

E5.justification: Both versions state that results summarize three seeds using means and standard deviations. v2 adds limited seed disclosure by identifying an example run as seed 2024 in Figure 5. No increased independent-run count, new confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedure is established.

E6.justification: The original classification scores are retained, but substantial new results are reported. Examples include ANFR's 76.34 on Fed-ISIC2019 with doubled local steps and 83.20 on CIFAR-10 with random initialization. Broader comparisons also reveal exceptions to overall superiority: Table 9 reports 78.32 for FedConv-InvertUp versus 75.07 for ANFR-ECA on Fed-ISIC2019. These are added comparisons under specified conditions, not revised same-setting gains.

T1.justification: v2 omits v1's explicit definition of the sample-weighted global objective in Equation 1 while retaining the local objective and core normalization/channel-descriptor derivations. Section 3.3 adds an assertion that ANFR inherits the aggregation method's convergence guarantees, without supplying new assumptions, a theorem, or a proof.

C1.justification: The central claims about combining weight standardization with channel attention, aggregation compatibility, and privacy utility remain. The novelty claim is narrowed: v1 says prior work had not designed heterogeneity-specific models and calls ANFR the first such broadly compatible method; v2 acknowledges FedConv and removes the conclusion's explicit 'first' claim.

C2.justification: v2 interprets baseline-tuned hyperparameters as yielding conservative performance estimates, discusses diminishing returns from increasing BN batch sizes, and adds accuracy/memory/latency tradeoffs relevant to resource constraints and stragglers. These extend the discussion while retaining the original channel-attention mechanism and DP-regularization interpretations.

D1.justification: v1 promises a future code release; v2 supplies a code-access link in the abstract. v2 also explicitly discloses the existing validation-based checkpoint-selection procedure and documents settings for the new training and profiling experiments, including profiler, batch size, mixed precision, and hardware information. Pretrained weights remain promised after acceptance.

R1.justification: v2 adds FedConv as directly relevant prior architectural work and revises the comparison matrix and novelty positioning accordingly. It also adds references for ViT, ConvNeXt, and EfficientNetV2 associated with the expanded evaluation. Most of the existing literature review and research positioning remain intact.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and interpretability discussion receive substantial editing. The formerly continuous method section becomes four named subsections, experiments are reorganized, and a new results appendix changes the appendix structure. The title and author information also change, and the standalone reproducibility statement is removed.

P2.justification: v2 adds seven tables and a four-panel convergence figure, expands the personalized-comparison table, and relocates the related-work matrix into the main text. The journal layout substantially resizes and reformats existing displays while retaining their image content. Table 10 also swaps the GFLOPs/GMACs headings relative to v1 Table 6 without changing the numerical entries.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens empirical scrutiny: the added architectural competitors address v1's narrow comparator scope, alternative initialization and training protocols test dependence on the original setup, and measured runtime/memory support assessment of practical utility. Code-access information and checkpoint-selection disclosure improve reproducibility. Important caveats remain: Table 9 does not support blanket superiority claims, and the no-early-stopping experiment changes other settings simultaneously. Nevertheless, the added evidence substantially improves readers' ability to assess ANFR's strengths and boundaries.
